title: address names a device's existing instances and the next free instance number
intention: address lists which instance numbers exist for a device (instances) and names the lowest unused one (next_free_instance), reading the instance root through its own ROOTS and creating nothing, so a caller that needs a second instance asks address and never globs devices/<device>/ itself.
why: Orchestrator ruling 2026-11-13 on ticket d13859e2ae46 (shim naming): shim.py must read instance directories through address, not glob devices/<device>/; address has instance_path, log_path, tool_path and machine_path but no function that lists instances. Akien, outline 5.3.5.2.2: 'we have a cc_0 instance, so I'll launch it with cc_1'.
traces_to: RULE 1 (encapsulation: the address tool owns instance directory layout) and CP1.
how: Add instances(device, roots=None) -> list[int] (sorted numeric directory names under <ROOTS['instance']>/devices/<device>, [] if absent, no mkdir) and next_free_instance(device, roots=None) -> int (lowest non-negative integer not in that list) to address.py. One proof over a scratch roots dict, one tooth per clause.

clauses.claim: instances(device, roots) returns the sorted integers of the numeric directories under <instance root>/devices/<device>, ignores non-numeric names, returns [] when the folder is absent, and creates nothing
next_free_instance(device, roots) returns the lowest non-negative integer not among instances(): [0, 2] gives 1, [] gives 0, [0, 1, 2] gives 3

decisions.text: D1: two read-only functions in address.py; a directory counts as an instance whether or not its process runs.
D2: one proof over a scratch roots dict, one tooth per clause; red first.

measured.saw: address.py defines instance_path (line 127), log_path, tool_path, held_tool_paths and machine_path, and no function that lists instances; shim.py's instance is the diagnostic attribute diagnostic_instance (default 0, diagnostic.py:146), not a value the shim chooses.
measured.how: grep -n '^def ' cairn/tools/base/address.py; grep -n diagnostic_instance cairn/tools/base/shim.py cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py
